episodes.title: What Is Outbreak Science?
episodes.description: Introduce infectious disease and the concepts needed to understand outbreaks, from microscopic processes to their effects on society.

episodes.title: How Do Outbreaks Start?
episodes.description: You may not realize it, but your body is like a fortress, designed to defend you from tiny foreign invaders known as pathogens.

episodes.title: Why Do We Have Fewer Outbreaks? Epidemiological Transition
episodes.description: Explore epidemiological transition and how societies have improved their responses to infectious diseases over time.

episodes.title: Why Do Outbreaks Affect People Unequally?
episodes.description: Investigate how inequalities within and between communities shape people’s risk during outbreaks.

episodes.title: The Weaponization of Outbreaks
episodes.description: Examine historical uses of outbreaks to deliberately harm people and lessons for preventing biological attacks.

episodes.title: How Do We Know We’re Sick?
episodes.description: Use symptoms and diagnostic tests to investigate hypothetical patients’ illnesses and understand how diagnosis helps limit disease spread.

episodes.title: How Does the Healthcare System Work During Outbreaks?
episodes.description: Explore how healthcare facilities respond to outbreaks, including staffing, resources, and costs.

episodes.title: How Do We Investigate Outbreaks? Epidemiology
episodes.description: Explore how epidemiology tracks relationships between people and infectious disease to investigate and help stop outbreaks.

episodes.title: Can We Predict An Outbreak’s Future? – Modeling
episodes.description: Use models and simulations to investigate how outbreaks might unfold under different conditions.

episodes.title: How Does Public Health Tackle Outbreaks?
episodes.description: Public health activities are all the ways society coordinates to deliver better health to people.

episodes.title: How Can Cooperation End an Outbreak?
episodes.description: In 1959, the WHO set out to eradicate smallpox, an ambitious goal that was achieved by 1980.

episodes.title: How Can Infrastructure Help Us Stop Outbreaks?
episodes.description: Explore sanitation technologies, including toilets, and their role in preventing outbreaks.

episodes.title: What Is Outbreak Culture?
episodes.description: Culture determines how we collaborate and use the resources at our disposal in the face of an outbreak.

episodes.title: How do Outbreaks End? Vaccines and Recovery
episodes.description: Explore vaccines and other outbreak-response tools, along with recovery work after an outbreak ends.

episodes.title: How Are We All Part of Ending Outbreaks?
episodes.description: Because outbreak science is an interdisciplinary field, everyone has a role to play in ending outbreaks, including you!
